text:
kelly: Escalation - customer (corp-acme) reporting intermittent 502s and timeouts on hosted inference around our cert rotation window (03:12 UTC). They see a pattern of a few hundred failed requests over ~4m with TCP resets and TLS handshake timeouts. Paste from their client logs: 

  [2026-04-01T03:12:05Z] ERROR request id=abc123 status=502 err=upstream reset by peer
  [2026-04-01T03:12:06Z] WARN handshake timeout after 5s
  [2026-04-01T03:12:07Z] ERROR socket closed before read

  I also captured traces from our gateway on the same time window, looks like frontends restarted during cert install. Can infra take a look? @infra-oncall

aj: Thanks. Can you attach the customer request IDs and the gateway trace ids? Also what region?

kelly: Sent DM with request ids and trace ids. Region: us-west-2. Customer is using our hosted endpoint (api.redwood.ai/v1/generate). They did not change DNS or client config.

sre-bot: Alert: spike detected - gateway-frontend-usw2 TLS connections 502-rate +340% at 03:12:02 UTC. Rolling window 5m.

infra-oncall: grabbing gateway traces now. Quick note: our cert rotation job started at 03:11:58 and completed 03:12:18. I'm seeing a handful of frontends that momentarily dropped existing sockets while swapping keys (graceful restart not clean). Attaching tcpdump snippet: 

  03:12:03.122 IP client > gw: Flags [S], seq 0 
  03:12:03.125 IP gw > client: Flags [R], seq 1 
  03:12:03.126 IP client > gw: Flags [S], seq 0 
  03:12:03.630 IP client > gw: Flags [S], seq 0 
  03:12:04.100 IP gw > client: Flags [RST, ACK] 

samir: Interesting — this looks like an "ephemeral socket blackhole" where the socket is accepted by one process, then during cert swap the listener dies or handoff fails and the kernel RSTs. That results in client seeing reset or handshake timeout depending on timing.

maria: I reproduced locally by triggering cert reload and hammering with: 

  while true; do curl -sv --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:10.0.0.5 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health || echo fail; done

  while simultaneously running: 
  sudo systemctl restart gateway-frontend && tcpdump -n -i any 'tcp port 443' -w /tmp/trace.pcap

  Repro is flaky but present with our current zero-downtime reload code path.

aj: Any DNS/resolver involvement? Customer also reported some older clients hitting stale IPs during the same window. Could be partial propagation + cert rotate.

infra-oncall: Checking. We did a small IP failover for a handful of frontends 03:11:55 -> 03:12:05 due to placement. DNS TTL for some internal LB entries was low (30s), but some external resolvers had cached previous IPs. So a mix of old IPs + in-place cert swap looks plausible.

support-bot: Customer updated: "we saw a repeatable spike when you rotated certs, about ~1.2% of our requests failed for ~3-5m. We've rolled out a retry with linear backoff for now."

maria: Short-term mitigations: 
  - Pause cert rotation rolling waves and extend the staging window to 10m while we fix reload handshake (deploy change that avoids killing listener). 
  - Add a readiness delay so sockets drain for 30s before process stops. 
  - Advise support to tell customers to implement idempotent retry (we already do 3 retries on SDK but not enforced).

samir: Long-term: improve hot-reload path to not transiently RST sockets; also consider serving the TLS cert from shared file descriptor (SO_REUSEPORT handoff) or use sidecar TLS that can rotate without killing frontend processes.

aj: Created ticket INFRA-8762 to track immediate rollback of the bleeding release and the hotfix for graceful reload. Assigning to @maria and @samir.

kelly: Customer accepted mitigation plan and wants timeline. Can we give ETA for hotfix + window extension?

maria: I can push a rollback-safe hotfix in ~3 hours (will add draining delay + config flag to rollback). If QA passes, we can re-run cert rotation with extended staging tomorrow morning low-traffic window.

infra-oncall: For the incident graph - I'll mark it as resolved after we complete the rollback. I'll also open a postmortem doc.

support-bot: Customer follow-up: "Thanks, please let us know when rotation is done and we'll monitor. We appreciate the quick triage." :thumbsup:

samir: notes for runbook update: add explicit check for in-flight sockets before SIGHUP sequence; add DNS check step to ensure no cross-IP propagation in rotation window.

kelly: closing loop here — will update customer after rollback. tagging this thread to the postmortem once it's created. Thanks all. :heart:
